title: Kiss of the Spiderwoman - musical theatre review - a theatrical triumph
transcript: Hello and welcome to Theatre Reviews with Paul Severn. I'm here at the Mast Southampton to see Kiss of the Spider Woman. >> >> John Kander and Fred Ebb are best known for writing Cabaret and Chicago. Their musical Kiss of the Spider Woman is far less familiar. Adapted from the novel by Manuel Puig, it premiered in the West End in 1992 before transferring to Broadway in 1993 where it won seven Tony Awards. I can't believe it's not performed more often. The score, infused with evocative Latin rhythms, stirs deep emotions while the story is profoundly moving. Not to mention harrowing. Stay with me and I'll tell you more about this superb production co-produced by Bristol Old Vic, the Leicester Curve, and the Mast Southampton. I caught it at that latter venue, the final stop of an inexplicably short tour. But first, please like, comment, and subscribe to this channel. And if you want to read these reviews and my roundups of other critics' reviews, please go to theatre.reviews. This revival is far more intimate than the apparently spectacular premiere over 30 years ago. But it's not a cut-price version by any means. The set entirely befits what is ultimately a love story. The setting is a prison cell in 1970s Argentina shared by Valentin, a political prisoner, and Molina, a gay man. These were dark times in that country under the governments of Juan Peron's widow and then a military junta. Yeah, you'll remember General Galtieri from the Falklands War. Uh trade unionists, left-wingers, and the people faced imprisonment, torture, or notoriously became the disappeared. Seeking refuge from the brutality of prison life, Molina, uh played by Fabian Soto Pacheco, and wearing soft feminine clothes, transports himself to his childhood memories of movies featuring a screen goddess called Aurora. As he recounts the plots of these films, Aurora materializes before us singing and dancing. David Woodhead said, "Brilliantly contrast the austere grayness of the cell and its two narrow beds and floor-to-ceiling iron bars with the colorful glamour of Aurora and her fabulous costumes, uh designed by Gabriella Slade. She appears as a mature woman, uh presumably reflecting the child's perception of the movie star as much older than himself. Anna-Jane Casey is charismatic in the role, commanding the stage with her swaggering dance and her seductive smile." Projected at the back of the stage are scenes from her black-and-white movies, cleverly created by Andre Golding. Uh George Blagden delivers a compelling performance as Valentin. Um As an idealistic revolutionary and a heterosexual, he's initially indifferent or even hostile to Molina, but comes to value the escape into beauty and love as the latter describes it. The movies and their songs become more meaningful to him than his ideological book that he reads by Karl Marx. Both performers sing and act well. Uh Molina is uh vulnerable and pragmatic. Valentin, tough and principled. Although both remain attached to loved ones outside the prison walls, their love for each other grows as each recognizes and appreciates the strength of the other. Inevitably, we think of fluidity of gender and sexuality. The prison authorities attempt to exploit this developing relationship to pressure Molina into extracting information about Valentine's associates. What follows then is a is a gripping struggle within Molina between love and self-preservation. Throughout the movies, a metaphor for art in general, not only provide escape from life, but a blueprint for how to live. All the acting is top-class, but I'll mention Jay Rincon as the cunning and sadistic prison warder. His chilling performance sends a shudder down the spine and makes these scenes of violence that much more believable. This production, directed by Paul Foster, serves as a timely reminder to people like me who spend most of our time in London theaters that regional productions can be as artistically accomplished, emotionally powerful, and theatrically thrilling as anything the capital has to offer. I give Kiss of the Spider Woman five stars. >> >> I hope you enjoyed this review or at least found it useful. And if you did, please like, comment, and subscribe to this channel. Well, then you'll be the first to know about my future reviews. And you can read my reviews and my roundups of other critics' reviews at my website, theater.reviews. You can also find me on social media like Threads, Mastodon, and Instagram. Thank you for watching.
